answer: A slashable stake ledger resists Sybil attacks: each agent locks collateral tied to one hardware attestation, and voting weight grows with the square root of the bond. Many keys from one actor add no influence, since weight follows total stake, not headcount, and fraud burns the bond. A tide feeding a shared lagoon lifts the level only by what each deposit adds, so a pretender must bring real value. The fable of a thousand borrowed names fails because empty accounts weigh nothing, and a tenth of the votes costs roughly a hundred times an honest stake, forfeited on first proof of cheating.
